---
title: Share a graphic
description: Save a graphic as a .fjgraphic file with the fonts and pictures it uses, and bring one into another project.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A `.fjgraphic` file carries one graphic, with the fonts and pictures it uses, so you can move it to another project or give it to someone else with Frame Job. Finder calls the file a Frame Job Graphic.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
  where={['Export… and From File… in the Insert Graphic sheet', 'A .fjgraphic opened from the Finder']}
  tools={['export_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
/>

## Export a graphic

<Steps>

1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…** and pick the graphic in the Insert Graphic sheet. It can be a bundled template or one from **This Project**.

2. Choose **Export…**. It's dimmed when the chosen graphic doesn't compile, and while another export is running.

3. In the save panel, which slides down over the sheet with `<module>.fjgraphic` as the name, choose where to put the file and save.

</Steps>

The Insert Graphic sheet stays open. The line under its lists says `Exporting <title>…`, then `Exported <title> to <file>:` followed by the files the package holds, or says why it couldn't.

Saving over an existing file replaces it whole. If the export fails, the file already there is left as it was.

Exporting changes nothing in the project and isn't an undo step.

## What a package packs

A package holds the module and only the project fonts and pictures the graphic uses. To find those, Frame Job draws the graphic and packs what it saw used:

- Every frame with the default properties. A graphic longer than 900 frames has 900 frames spread evenly over it.
- Then each choice of each [Enum](/graphics/properties/#enum) property and the other value of each [Boolean](/graphics/properties/#boolean) property, one at a time, over 30 frames each. It draws at most 32 of these.

A font is packed when the graphic drew or measured text with it, or fell back to it for a character its own font lacks. A picture is packed when the graphic's `asset(name)` drew it. The app's own fonts are never packed, because every copy of Frame Job has them, so a bundled template's package holds its module and nothing else.

A frame that fails to draw is skipped.

:::caution
[String](/graphics/properties/#string) and [Asset](/graphics/properties/#asset) properties are only tried at their defaults. A font or picture the graphic reaches only through another value, such as a different title or another picture, isn't packed. Read the file list in the message line after an export, and if something's missing, make it that property's default in the module and export again.
:::

## The .fjgraphic file

A package is a zip with nothing compressed. It holds `manifest.json`, the module, and the `fonts/` and `assets/` folders. The manifest gives the package's format, the module, its title, category and description, the Frame Job version that wrote it, and each file's path, name, size and SHA-256.

Exporting the same graphic twice with the same version of Frame Job gives byte-identical files.

A file name a zip path can't hold is stored under a tidied name. That covers a `:` or `\`, a control character and a leading `.`, so `a:b.ttf` is stored as `a-b.ttf`. The manifest keeps the original, so a font is still found by its family and `asset(name)` still finds its picture.

A package can hold at most about 4 GiB and 65,535 files.

## Open from the Finder

Double-click a `.fjgraphic`, open it with **Open With**, drop it on Frame Job's Dock icon, or open it from a browser's downloads. Frame Job [checks the package](#package-checks), then puts up the [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet).

The package goes into the front project, the one whose window is in front. With no project open, it goes into a new untitled project. A package that fails its checks before the sheet appears shows an alert and opens no project.

If Frame Job wasn't running, it opens first and the package waits until any projects it reopens are back, so it lands once, in one project, with no Welcome window.

**File ▸ Open** doesn't list `.fjgraphic` files, and there's no menu item for importing one.

## Import with From File…

<Steps>

1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**. The Insert Graphic sheet closes and a file panel opens.

2. Choose a `.fjgraphic`. The [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet) appears for that same project.

</Steps>

The panel also takes a `.js` module, which goes straight onto the timeline. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

## The Import Graphic sheet

Before anything is copied, the sheet shows the graphic's title and description, then what will happen to each file:

| Line | What it can read |
| --- | --- |
| Module | `Module: lower-third`, `Module: lower-third (already in this project)`, or `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)` |
| Fonts | The font files, each plain, marked `(already here)`, or marked `(as Inter-2.ttf)`. With none, `Fonts: none`. |
| Pictures | The picture files, each plain or marked `(already here)`. With none, `Pictures: none`. |

Under them it says "Importing copies these files into this project's graphics. It is not an Undo step."

Choose **Import** to copy the files, or **Cancel** to copy nothing.

If the project's graphics folder changed while the sheet was up and the import can't go ahead, Frame Job beeps, the sheet stays open and it says why.

## Name clashes

An import never replaces a file. Each file keeps the name the package gives it, unless that name is taken:

| The project already has | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| A file of that name with the same contents | It's used as it is, and the sheet says "already here". |
| A different module of that name | The module is copied under a new name with `-2`, `-3` and so on: `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)`. |
| A different font of that name | The font is copied under a new name, such as `as Inter-2.ttf`. A font is found by its family, so its file name changes nothing. |
| A different picture of that name | The import stops, because the module asks for its pictures by name. An alert says so. Rename or remove the project's file and import again. |

A name that differs only in case counts as taken. A module name also counts as taken while clips left behind by a [deleted graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/) still use it.

To find the project's pictures, see [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

## After an import

**Import** copies the files into the project's graphics folder and opens the Insert Graphic sheet on **This Project** with the graphic chosen, ready to insert. The line under the lists says what happened:

`Imported Lower third as lower-third. Added: lower-third.js, fonts/Inter.ttf. Already here: assets/logo.png.`

An import only copies files. It places no clip, so choose **Insert** when you want one on the timeline.

Importing isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. An untitled project keeps the files when it's first saved. If a copy fails part-way, what it had copied is removed.

## Package checks

Frame Job checks a package before it copies anything, and a check that fails writes nothing. The message reads `<file> cannot be imported:` followed by the reason.

| What's wrong | What the reason says |
| --- | --- |
| The file is empty | `it is empty (0 bytes)` |
| It isn't a zip, or it's damaged | For example `the package is not a zip: no end of central directory record` |
| It was compressed, for example by zipping it again | `<entry> is compressed (method 8); a .fjgraphic holds stored entries only` |
| It was changed after it was written | The entry that differs from the manifest by path, size or SHA-256, such as `<entry> is 2048 bytes, but the manifest says 1024` |
| A newer Frame Job wrote it | `the package is format 2; this Frame Job reads format 1`, and that a newer Frame Job wrote it |
| A font is bad | `the font "<name>" is not a .ttf or .otf file`, or why it doesn't load |
| A picture is bad | `the picture "<name>"` and why: it isn't a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file, its name can't be used, or it's empty |

A module that doesn't compile passes these checks and is imported. It's listed on **This Project** with **Export…** dimmed, and **Insert** places nothing and shows the first error. Fix it the way you'd fix any module. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).

## With an agent

`export_graphic` is **Export…**, writing to a path instead of through a save panel, and it also says how many frames it drew and how many failed. The assistant asks you before it runs, because it can replace a file.

`import_graphic` is **Import** without the sheet, so nothing asks first. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

## Related

- [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/)
- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
- [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/)
- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)

---
title: The Graphic sub-tab
description: See which module draws a graphic clip, open it in your editor, and read what it reports when it doesn't draw as it should.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Select a graphic clip and the inspector's **Clip** tab gains a **Graphic** sub-tab. It's where you set what the graphic shows, see which module draws it, and find out what's wrong when it doesn't draw as it should.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic" tools={['set_graphic', 'get_graphic']} />

<Shot
  name="07-clip-graphic.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with a graphic clip selected. Graphic, Picture and Clip sub-tabs sit above four sections. Source is collapsed and reads Lower third. Properties is open with six rows: Title, subtitle, accent, size, boxed and align. Size is collapsed and reads 960 × 540, and Timeline is collapsed and reads 00:00:05:00."
/>

## The Graphic sub-tab

A graphic clip's sub-tabs are **Graphic**, **Picture** and **Clip**, in that order. **Graphic** appears only when every selected clip is a graphic clip, so any other kind of clip in the selection removes it.

| Section | What it's for | Summary when collapsed | Starts | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Source](#source) | What draws the clip, and what the module reports about it | The error or warning count, or the module's name | Collapsed | Always |
| [Properties](/graphics/properties/) | What the graphic shows | The number of properties | Open | When every selected clip is drawn by one module |
| [Size](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's width and height | `W × H` | Collapsed | Always |
| [Timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's own timeline | Its length | Collapsed | With one clip selected |

There's no **Color** sub-tab. To grade a graphic, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above it.

## The Picture sub-tab

A graphic has the same layer settings as other clips, so you can move, scale and fade it: [Transform](/canvas/transform/) (position, scale, rotation and opacity), [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/), [Shadow](/effects/shadow/), [Filters](/effects/filters/), [Reflection](/effects/reflection/), [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) and [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).

It has no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key, which are for clips drawn from media.

## The Clip sub-tab

**Clip** has the clip's [Timing](/editing/timing-section/) when one clip is selected, [Transition](/motion/transition-settings/) when the clip overlaps the one before it, and [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

There's no Speed section. A graphic has no speed control or speed ramp, because its timing comes from the module and its [Length](/graphics/size-and-timing/).

## Source

Source says what draws the clip. Its summary, when collapsed, is `1 error` or `2 warnings` if there's anything to report, and otherwise the module's name.

### Name, File and Revision

| Row | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | The module's display name, or its file name when it has none |
| **File** | The module's file, `<name>.js` |
| **Revision** | The first eight characters of the SHA-256 of the file's text, which change whenever the text does, or `missing` when the file is gone |

### Open in Editor

**Open in Editor** opens the module in the app your Mac uses for `.js` files. Save there and the preview redraws within a moment. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).

### Reveal in Finder

**Reveal in Finder** shows the module's file in a Finder window.

Below these two, **Duplicate as New Graphic…** makes a copy of the module for the selected clips. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

## Diagnostics

Under the buttons, Source lists what the module says about the clip, under a heading for each stage:

- **Compiling the module** appears when there's something to report: the compile error, or the warnings the module's top level gave.
- **No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame** means that frame drew cleanly. **Checked at the clip's first frame** is followed by what that frame reported. Neither appears when the module didn't compile.

The first frame is drawn at the clip's own size, so a missing font, a picture that isn't in the project or a size mismatch shows here. With several clips of one module selected, the check is of the first of them.

Each row reads `line L, column C — message`, or the message alone when it has no place in the file. An error is in the strong ink and a warning is muted.

While you drag a control, the list holds still. It updates when you let go.

### Open a diagnostic

Click a diagnostic, or its **Open** button, to open the module in your editor. This opens the file, not the line, so note the line number first.

### In the graphics folder

**In the graphics folder** lists what Frame Job skipped or couldn't watch when it scanned the project's graphics folder:

- A module or picture with a bad name.
- An empty file.
- A font that loads no face.
- A file that couldn't be watched.

Each row has a **Reveal** button, and clicking it or the row shows the graphics folder in Finder, not the file. These rows count as warnings in the section's summary.

## A missing module

When the module's file is gone, **Open in Editor**, **Reveal in Finder** and **Duplicate as New Graphic…** are disabled, **Revision** reads `missing`, and Source shows the error `No module named "<name>" in graphics/`.

If Frame Job kept an earlier version, you can [restore it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

## Several modules selected

When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, Source's summary counts them, such as `2 modules`. It names them and says:

> Drawn by different modules: lower-third, title-card
>
> Select one module's clips to edit its properties.

The rows, buttons and diagnostics are gone until you do. **Size** stays editable, because it doesn't depend on the module. **Properties** needs one module and **Timeline** needs one clip.

## Switching clips to another module

The inspector can't point clips at a different module that already exists. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches them to a new copy.

To move clips to an existing module, delete them and [insert that module](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) again, or have an agent do it with `set_graphic`.

## Related

- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
- [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/)

Properties appears only when all the selected clips share one module. Clips of different modules can't be edited together, and an agent can't set their properties in one go either. See [Several modules selected](/graphics/graphic-tab/#several-modules-selected).

## Stale values

A clip can hold a value for a property the module no longer declares, for example after you rename a property in the module. The value stays, listed below the rows with its key dimmed, its value beside it, and **⌫** to remove it.

The clip still draws. The value is passed to the module, and Source shows the warning `props.<key> is not in the schema; it is passed through`.

**⌫** removes the value from every selected clip, as one undo step named **Remove Graphic Property**.

With no compiled module, every stored value is listed this way. An action's end has stale rows of its own, marked as the action's. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

## Good to know

A stored value that no longer suits its property, such as a choice the module has dropped from an [Enum](#enum), isn't listed as stale. The clip draws the module's default, and Source shows a warning naming the property.
